_doc: Maps each ingredientKey (matching /library/ingredient-yields/<slug>/) to its native identifier in each public price source. The CI/prod fetch worker reads this to resolve what to pull; the composite engine (tools/_shared/composite-price.js) decides LEVEL vs TREND by basis. EVERY id here is an UNVERIFIED best-guess (verified:false) per the API-integration spec — resolve each against the source's discovery endpoint (AMS /reports, BLS series directory, FRED /series/search, NOAA FOSS species list) and flip verified:true before it ships behind the fact-gate. basis mapping: ams=wholesale level, noaa=wholesale (ex-vessel) level, fred=level or index per its 'basis', bls=index (trend-only). A missing source key = that source is simply skipped for that ingredient; "" = known to have none. ams.reportId is the NUMERIC MARS slug_id (find it with `node scripts/verify-cost-index-sources.mjs --discover <term>` — the report slug like LM_XB403 404s). ams.commodity filters a multi-commodity report (e.g. a terminal 'Vegetables' report) down to one ingredient's rows (field-agnostic match). _report is a human label, ignored by code. Produce uses the Baltimore terminal (DMV market); chicken uses the National Chicken Report. Beef/pork (ribeye, tenderloin, pork-*) still carry LMR slugs (LM_XB403/LM_PK602) — the boxed-beef/negotiated-pork wholesale reports aren't in the Market News v1.2 directory, so confirm whether they need the separate LMR/Datamart API. See scripts/check-cost-index-sources.mjs (shape + alignment validator, warns on unverified) and the 'Cost Index — API Integration Architecture' section of the plan.
